known_differences.description: fsci-fft uses naive O(n^2) DFT; SciPy uses PocketFFT with Bluestein/Rader for non-power-of-2 sizes. Numerical results may differ at machine epsilon level.

threats.description: NaN or Inf values in complex input arrays propagate through DFT summation, corrupting all output bins. A single non-finite input element can render the entire transform result unusable.
threats.mitigation: When check_finite is enabled or in Hardened mode, scan input for non-finite values before transform. Return NonFiniteInput error immediately.
threats.strict_mode_response: Check finiteness when check_finite flag is set.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Always check finiteness regardless of flag.

threats.description: Naive O(n^2) DFT implementation becomes extremely slow for large inputs. A 2^20 element transform requires ~10^12 floating-point operations, making denial-of-service trivial via large input arrays.
threats.mitigation: Document performance characteristics. Future: implement Cooley-Tukey FFT for O(n log n) performance. Consider input size limits for resource-constrained environments.
threats.strict_mode_response: Allow large transforms with performance warning in trace.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Same behavior; no hard size limit currently enforced.

threats.description: Zero or negative sample spacing in fftfreq/rfftfreq produces nonsensical frequency values or division by zero.
threats.mitigation: Validate sample_spacing > 0 and finite before computation. Return NonPositiveSampleSpacing error.
threats.strict_mode_response: Error: 'sample spacing must be finite and greater than zero'.

threats.description: Empty input arrays cause index-out-of-bounds or nonsensical zero-length output. Must be rejected before entering transform loop.
threats.mitigation: Validate input length > 0 before any transform. Return InvalidShape error.
threats.strict_mode_response: Error: 'input length must be greater than zero'.
threats.hardened_mode_response: Same error; input validation is unconditional.
